title: Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner growth model

source.title: Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner growth model

notes: Published in [*Electronic Journal of Probability* **31** (2026), 1–35](https://doi.org/10.1214/26-EJP1634). The map's result numbers and source locations follow the accepted manuscript of 31 October 2026. [The earlier arXiv v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08757v2) has different numbering in Section 3.
Read the guide for the main results in the paper’s order and for differences in the Lean proofs.

results.summary: Explains how the moment hypotheses used here compare with the hypotheses of the cited limit-shape results.

coverage.scope: This item gives context for the results in the paper.

results.label: Lemma 2.6
results.title: Negative tilt and the shape superdifferential
results.summary: The negative tilt is almost surely a supergradient at some interior direction. If its mean is a supergradient at a fixed direction, so is the negative tilt almost surely. If the mean is an extreme point of that superdifferential, the tilt is almost surely constant.
results.notes: This result is quoted from Busemann functions and Gibbs measures in directed polymer models on $\mathbb Z^2$, Lemma 4.5, in the zero-temperature setting.

coverage.scope: Lean proves all three conclusions for the planar model.

results.label: Theorem 2.7
results.title: A Busemann process on an extended space
results.summary: Constructs both Busemann fields for every negative supporting slope of the limit shape on a probability space that carries the weights and extra variables.
results.notes: The construction is the zero-temperature case of Janjigian and Rassoul-Agha, Busemann functions and Gibbs measures in directed polymer models on $\mathbb Z^2$, Theorem 4.7 in the journal and Theorem 4.8 in arXiv v3.

coverage.scope: Lean proves all six clauses. Fixed-tilt agreement supplies the equality case of the order clause because the first coordinate determines the tilt. The linked results verify continuity of the shifts and identify the full tilt index set.

links.label: Equal first coordinates give equal tilts
No finite supporting slope on the axes

results.label: Remark 2.8
results.title: Backward independence convention
results.summary: Records the backward-independence convention for the process on an extended probability space.

coverage.scope: This item gives context for the results in the paper.

results.label: Remark 2.9
results.title: Direction versus tilt indexing
results.summary: Direction indexing uses only the negatives of the extreme points of each directional superdifferential. The two index sets agree if the shape is differentiable at every interior direction.

coverage.scope: This item gives context for the results in the paper.

results.label: Theorem 2.11
results.title: Coalescence for the extended-space process
results.summary: For each fixed tilt in the extended-space process, almost surely the rightmost cocycle geodesics from all starting sites coalesce.
results.notes: The proof is cited from Geodesics and the competition interface for the corner growth model, Theorem A.1 of arXiv:1510.00860v1.

coverage.scope: The certificate covers both branches at each fixed tilt in the extended-space process.

results.label: Remark 2.13
results.title: Forward measurability as adaptedness
results.summary: Interprets measurability from weights northeast of a site as measurability with respect to a forward filtration.

coverage.scope: This item gives context for the results in the paper.

results.label: Remark 2.16
results.title: Geodesic-system terminology
results.summary: Compares the name for a covariant coalescing family of random geodesics with terminology in first-passage percolation.

coverage.scope: This item gives context for the results in the paper.

results.label: Lemma 2.17
results.title: Covariance of the generated cocycle
results.summary: A shift-covariant coalescing geodesic system generates a shift-covariant Busemann cocycle.

results.label: Theorem 3.1
results.title: Strong existence at a deterministic tilt
results.summary: A generalized Busemann cocycle with coalescing rightmost geodesics and almost surely constant tilt agrees almost surely with a forward-measurable cocycle on the weight space, evaluated at the same weights.
definitions: Forward measurability means that $B(x,y)$ for $x,y\in u+\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$ depends measurably on $\{\omega_z:z\in u+\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2\}$.

coverage.scope: The certificate proves the equality for all pairs of sites on one probability-one event on the specified space.

restriction.label: Specified extended space
restriction.paper_scope: Any Polish probability space carrying the weights and equipped with the paper’s shift action.
restriction.certified_scope: The space $\Omega\times\mathbb R^{\mathbb N\times\mathbb Z^2\times\{1,2\}}$ with the coordinate shifts and any invariant law with the prescribed weight marginal on $\Omega$.
restriction.gap: Representation on arbitrary extensions satisfying the paper’s hypotheses.
restriction.reason: The certificate takes the space and its shifts as fixed inputs to the conditional path law construction.
restriction.impact: This space carries the cocycles used to realize the negatives of the extreme points in Proposition 3.6.

results.label: Remark 3.2
results.title: Criterion for strong existence
results.summary: A coalescing cocycle has a version measurable from the weights exactly when its tilt is almost surely constant. This holds when the negative mean tilt is an extreme point of a directional superdifferential.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 3.3
results.title: A deterministic projection fixes the tilt
results.summary: If the projection of the random tilt along a nonzero vector with opposite weak coordinate signs is almost surely constant, the entire tilt is almost surely constant.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Remark 3.4
results.title: Queueing examples for the projection criterion
results.summary: Points to queueing fixed points that give cocycles with a deterministic expected-increment coordinate.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Theorem 3.5
results.title: Strong uniqueness and ordering
results.summary: Two cocycles on the weight space with coalescing rightmost geodesics are almost surely equal if their tilts agree. Otherwise they are almost surely strictly ordered in the same direction as their tilts.
definitions: The order $B_1\preceq B_2$ means $B_1(x,x+e_1)\geq B_2(x,x+e_1)$ and $B_1(x,x+e_2)\leq B_2(x,x+e_2)$ for all $x\in\mathbb Z^2$. Strict order additionally requires $B_1\ne B_2$.

coverage.scope: Lean proves almost-sure equality at equal tilts and weak order of the increments. The almost-sure strict order at distinct tilts remains to be checked against the certificates.

results.label: Remark 3.7
results.title: Possible gaps in H
results.summary: Asks whether either inclusion in Proposition 3.6 can be strict.
results.notes: This is a question about the geometry of the tilt set.

results.label: Example 3.8
results.title: Mixture with random tilt
results.summary: Constructs an extended-space cocycle by mixing two canonical cocycles with a Bernoulli selector, yielding a nonconstant tilt.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Remark 3.9
results.title: Mean tilt outside H
results.summary: Uses the mixture example to show that a nonattainable average tilt prevents a weight-measurable version.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Remark 3.10
results.title: Attainable interior tilt with random tilt
results.summary: Shows that an attainable interior point of a supergradient segment can still arise as the mean of a nonconstant random tilt.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Theorem 3.11
results.title: Strong existence of the tilt-indexed process
results.summary: There are left and right Busemann fields on the weight space for every tilt in $\mathcal H$. The two branches agree almost surely at each fixed tilt. Any two processes with the stated properties agree almost surely for every tilt, sign and pair of sites simultaneously.
definitions: Forward measurability means that $B(x,y)$ for $x,y\in u+\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$ depends measurably on $\{\omega_z:z\in u+\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2\}$.

coverage.scope: Lean proves the process theorem with the equal-index order clause handled by fixed-tilt agreement. It also proves that the same fields admit a measurable Skorokhod realization.

links.label: Strong existence and uniqueness of the process

results.label: Remark 3.12
results.title: Restrictions of process uniqueness
results.summary: Uniqueness also holds for the process indexed by negatives of extreme points and for a finite set of tilts.

coverage.scope: This item gives context for the results in the paper.

results.label: Remark 3.13
results.title: Covariance of the full process
results.summary: States that translating the environment translates the full indexed family on a common event of probability one.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Corollary 3.14
results.title: Strong mixing of the process
results.summary: For a fixed event of the weights and an event of the full process, the joint probability tends to the product of their probabilities as the latter event is shifted repeatedly by any nonzero lattice vector.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Theorem 3.15
results.title: Ergodic decomposition of extended cocycles
results.summary: For an extended-space cocycle with coalescing rightmost geodesics, its tilt $h$ belongs to $\mathcal H$ almost surely and the cocycle agrees with both canonical fields $B^{h-}$ and $B^{h+}$ at the same weights.
definitions: The tilt $h$ is the negative vector of conditional means of the origin increments $B(0,e_1),B(0,e_2)$ given the shift-invariant events. It can be random.

coverage.scope: The release covers the canonical process in Theorem 3.11. The representation at a general random tilt is outside its scope.

results.label: Remark 3.16
results.title: Interpretation of the decomposition
results.summary: The law of the tilt determines the mixture of canonical cocycles in the decomposition.

coverage.scope: This item gives context for the results in the paper.

results.label: Lemma 3.17
results.title: Uniqueness of cocycle geodesics
results.summary: For a coalescing generalized Busemann function, its rightmost path from each site is the only locally rightmost geodesic satisfying its cocycle rule.
definitions: A recovering cocycle satisfies $B(x,y)+B(y,z)=B(x,z)$ and $\min\{B(x,x+e_1),B(x,x+e_2)\}=\omega_x$. Its rightmost geodesic follows the smaller outgoing increment, choosing $e_1$ in a tie.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Theorem 3.18
results.title: Equivalence of geodesic and cocycle approaches
results.summary: The cocycle generated by a shift-covariant coalescing family recovers the original family. Under ergodicity the cocycle is shift-covariant, recovering and integrable, and its rightmost geodesics coalesce.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Remark 3.19
results.title: Integrability can fail without ergodicity
results.summary: An extended-space mixture of canonical fields with tilts approaching the axes can have an infinite first moment.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.1
results.title: Quantile-process properties
results.summary: Constructs a measurable path-valued quantile function from the conditional law of a cocycle geodesic and identifies its order with that conditional distribution.
definitions: For $s\in[0,1]$, a path quantile is the infimum of paths $\gamma$ for which the conditional probability that the original path lies weakly to the left of $\gamma$ is at least $s$.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Example 4.2
results.title: Finite-support quantile example
results.summary: Computes the quantile path when the conditional geodesic law has finite ordered support; the text says this example is not used later.
results.notes: The paper includes this as an illustration of the quantile definition.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.3
results.title: Conditional-law and quantile-law equality
results.summary: Shows that sampling a conditional Busemann geodesic has the same joint law with the environment as sampling the quantile process with an independent uniform level.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.4
results.title: Quantile sublevel equivalence for coalescing paths
results.summary: For coalescing reference paths, proves equality of the two quantile-process sublevel sets under a coalescing-geodesic hypothesis.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.5
results.title: Coalescence at almost every sampling level
results.summary: For almost every sampling level, the two corresponding paths from different roots eventually agree, with probability one.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.6
results.title: Paths determined by forward weights
results.summary: In a shift-covariant coalescing family of locally rightmost geodesics, each path can be read from the weights northeast of its starting point.
definitions: Two paths coalesce if they eventually take the same sequence of sites after meeting.
A locally rightmost geodesic is rightmost between its own pairs of sites.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.7
results.title: A cocycle from sampled paths
results.summary: At a positive sampling level for which paths from all roots coalesce almost surely, the paths give a stationary recovering cocycle. Its increments above a site depend only on weights northeast of that site.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.8
results.title: Geodesic-generated cocycle recovers the lifted cocycle
results.summary: Passage-time differences along any rightmost geodesic of a coalescing cocycle recover its values between every pair of lattice sites.

coverage.scope: For a recovering cocycle with coalescing rightmost geodesics, the passage-time difference along the path from any root eventually equals the cocycle increment. This applies for all lattice pairs on the same full-probability event as coalescence.

results.label: Lemma 4.9
results.title: Equality of weight and cocycle laws
results.summary: The original cocycle paired with the weight field has the same distribution as the cocycle from uniformly sampled quantile paths paired with the weight field.
definitions: The sampling level is drawn uniformly from $[0,1]$, independently of the weights.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.10
results.title: One cocycle for all positive sampling levels
results.summary: If the original tilt is deterministic, almost surely all sampling levels $s\in(0,1]$ give the same cocycle, with that tilt.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.11
results.title: Three-way comparison of cocycles
results.summary: Two canonical cocycles with coalescing rightmost geodesics are ordered in one direction, ordered in the other, or equal, almost surely.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Corollary 4.12
results.title: Coalescence and forward measurability
results.summary: A canonical recovering integrable cocycle has coalescing rightmost geodesics exactly when its increments are measurable from the forward weights.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.13
results.title: Ordering by tilt
results.summary: The canonical cocycles at two tilts are ordered almost surely in the same direction as the tilts.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 4.14
results.title: Identifying fixed-tilt limits
results.summary: At each fixed tilt, the extensions from the left and the right agree almost surely with the selected canonical cocycle.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 5.1
results.title: Uniqueness of covariant geodesic systems
results.summary: Two ordered noncrossing families of geodesics following the minimum increments of one cocycle agree almost surely under the stated coalescence and rightmost-path hypotheses.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 5.2
results.title: The cocycle-generated system recovers the given system
results.summary: For a shift-covariant coalescing geodesic system, its generated cocycle's right-tiebreaking geodesics agree with that system.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma 5.3
results.title: Generated cocycle belongs to the coalescing class
results.summary: Under ergodicity the cocycle generated by a shift-covariant coalescing geodesic family is integrable and its rightmost geodesics coalesce.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma A.1
results.title: Measurability of the conditional distribution
results.summary: The conditional probability that the B-geodesic lies below a path is jointly measurable in the environment and path.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Corollary A.2
results.title: Measurability of the quantile geodesic
results.summary: The path-valued quantile geodesic defined by the conditional path-order probability is measurable with respect to the weight sigma-field.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma A.3
results.title: A generating collection of path events
results.summary: The events that a path lies below a fixed path generate the Borel sigma-field on the rooted path space.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma A.4
results.title: Exclusion of a trivial B-geodesic
results.summary: With independent identically distributed weights of positive finite variance, the rightmost cocycle geodesic from a fixed site almost surely differs from both coordinate rays.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Theorem B.1
results.title: A cocycle from an infinite geodesic
results.summary: On one full-probability event, every semi-infinite geodesic escaping in both coordinates has finite Busemann limits to all lattice points, and these limits recover the weights.
definitions: For a semi-infinite geodesic $\pi$, the Busemann limit between $x$ and $y$ is $\lim_{n\to\infty}(L_{x,\pi_n}-L_{y,\pi_n})$ when the limit is finite.

coverage.scope: Lean gives that event and the finite recovering cocycle for every such geodesic when the weight law is nonconstant.

restriction.label: Weights with a nonconstant law
restriction.paper_scope: The appendix theorem assumes independent identically distributed weights with a finite moment of order greater than two. It gives one event of probability one on which all geodesics escaping in both coordinates generate finite recovering cocycles at every pair of lattice sites.
restriction.certified_scope: Lean gives that event and the finite recovering cocycle for every such geodesic when the weight law is nonconstant.
restriction.gap: The stated Lean theorem retains a nonconstant-law hypothesis. The point-mass case of this appendix statement is outside that declaration.
restriction.reason: The uniform finite-limit theorem takes the nonconstant-law hypothesis used by its geodesic comparison bounds.
restriction.impact: The model for the main Busemann process already assumes a nonconstant weight law, so this scope supplies its required finite-limit result.

links.label: Finite Busemann limits on a common event

results.label: Lemma B.2
results.title: Passage differences along a fixed geodesic
results.summary: For a fixed environment and a geodesic $\pi$ escaping in both coordinates, the difference $L_{x,\pi_n}-L_{\pi_k,\pi_n}$ has a nondecreasing limit for each $x$. Passage differences between points northeast of $\pi_k$ have finite limits.

coverage.scope: For fixed weights and any maximizing up-right geodesic tending to infinity in both coordinates, Lean proves the nondecreasing limit in $(-\infty,\infty]$ at every site and its finiteness in the northeast quadrant of the starting site. Subtracting the two finite limits gives the passage-time difference between any two sites in that quadrant.

results.label: Lemma B.3
results.title: Order of geodesic-generated cocycles
results.summary: Ordered nontrivial geodesics generate ordered cocycles; coalescing geodesics generate the same cocycle.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.

results.label: Lemma B.4
results.title: A coalescing cocycle is recovered by its paths
results.summary: If a recovering cocycle has a coalescing family of semi-infinite geodesics from every vertex, each path generates that same cocycle.

coverage.scope: For a recovering cocycle followed by a coalescing family from every site, the passage differences along each path eventually equal the corresponding cocycle increment. This stronger eventual equality directly gives the limiting claim.

results.label: Lemma B.5
results.title: A path between the two tie-breaking choices
results.summary: A nontrivial geodesic is a geodesic for its generated cocycle and lies between the e2- and e1-tiebreaking paths of that cocycle.

coverage.scope: The correspondence of this item with the Lean declarations has not been assessed.
